newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian landless leader convicted of murder.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian landless leader convicted of murder.

text.p: A leader of Brazil's radical Landless Movement (MST) was convicted of murder on Wednesday but will remain free pending an appeal, officials said.
A jury in the town of Pedro Canario, in Espirito Santo state, found Jose Rainha guilty of the 1989 ambush murders of a local farmer and a police officer, they said.
A judge sentenced the activist to 26 years in prison but said he could stay out of jail until September when the appeal was due to be held.

Rainha told reporters after the ruling he was being persecuted for political reasons. "The struggle will continue with ever more courage and determination because what we've seen here is how the landowners have swung this jury," he said.
Rainha, a senior member of the MST leadership, has organised dozens of invasions of unused private farmland by groups of landless workers.

Once an illiterate rural labourer, he rose quickly through the organisation's ranks and was in a delegation that met President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in April after a high-profile demonstration by the MST in Brasilia.

Despite that meeting, violent conflict over land continues to rack the Brazilian interior. In the latest clash on Sunday, two men died when an armed gang opened fire on a camp of landless workers in the northeastern state of Pernambuco.
